PaperTitle: Graph Embedding for Mapping Interdisciplinary Research Networks
Abstract:
Representation learning is the frst step in automating tasks such as research paper recommendation, classifcation, and retrieval. Due to the accelerating rate of research publication, together with the recognised benefts of interdisciplinary research, systems that facilitate researchers in discovering and understanding relevant works from beyond their immediate school of knowledge are vital. This work explores diferent methods of research paper representa

tion (or document embedding), to identify those methods that are capable of preserving the interdisciplinary implications of re

search papers in their embeddings. In addition to evaluating state of the art methods of document embedding in a interdisciplinary citation prediction task, we propose a novel Graph Neural Network architecture designed to preserve the key interdisciplinary impli

cations of research articles in citation network node embeddings. Our proposed method outperforms other GNN-based methods in interdisciplinary citation prediction, without compromising overall citation prediction performance.
SummaryAbstract: This paper addresses the challenge of discovering interdisciplinary research amidst accelerating publication rates by exploring various document embedding methods. The authors propose a novel Graph Neural Network architecture, ComBSAGE, designed to preserve the interdisciplinary implications of research articles in their embeddings. Their method outperforms other GNN-based approaches in interdisciplinary citation prediction without compromising overall performance.

References.PaperTitle: SciBERT: A Pretrained Language Model for Scientifc Text
References.Authors: Iz Beltagy, Kyle Lo, and Arman Cohan
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (EMNLP-IJCNLP)
References.SemanticInformation: This paper introduces SciBERT, a BERT-based model fine-tuned on a large corpus of scientific text from Semantic Scholar. The current paper utilizes SciBERT to encode the concatenated title and abstract of research papers, generating initial document embeddings. SciBERT serves as a key component for text-based representations and is evaluated as a baseline for document embedding performance, especially when no citation relations are known.

References.Publication: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artifcial Intelligence
References.SemanticInformation: This paper focuses on the over-smoothing problem in Graph Neural Networks, where node representations can converge and become indistinguishable from their neighbors. The proposed ComBSAGE method aims to mitigate this issue by its novel message aggregation approach, preserving distinct community signals.

References.PaperTitle: SPECTER: Document-level Representation Learning using Citation-informed Transformers
References.Authors: Arman Cohan, Sergey Feldman, Iz Beltagy, Doug Downey, and Daniel Weld
References.Publication: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
References.SemanticInformation: SPECTER is a method that fine-tunes text-based representations using citation relations as an inter-document signal. The current paper uses SPECTER as a baseline, initializing it with SciBERT and training it to minimize distance between citing and cited papers while maximizing distance from non-cited ones. It evaluates SPECTER's ability to predict both overall and interdisciplinary citations, positioning it on the spectrum of text and citation-based methods.
